title: Information security risk management
summary: Assess service consequences and choose proportionate treatments with accountable owners.
outcomes: Assess inherent, residual and target risk without false precision.
Maintain a treatment and acceptance cycle that informs decisions.

realExample.title: SARS uses automated risk selection
realExample.documentedOutcome: SARS's 2024/25 annual report describes automated risk selection for all verification cases and 88.41% of complex audits.
realExample.discussion: Discuss how a risk-based selection process focuses attention, and why the selection method, coverage and resulting decisions need review.
realExample.scope: A tax-compliance risk-management example. It is not presented as a measured cybersecurity control result.

units.title: Describe and assess the service risk
objectives: Connect a cause, event and consequence.
Use current controls and evidence in an assessment.

chapters.title: Write a risk that can be acted on
chapters.bodyHtml:
A useful risk statement connects a condition or cause, an uncertain event and a service consequence. 'Cyber risk is high' does not identify a decision. 'Because supplier support uses a shared privileged account, an unauthorised change could divert approved relief payments and delay assistance' gives an owner something to assess.

Separate the asset, threat and weakness. The payment record is the asset; a malicious actor or mistaken authorised user can be a source of harmful action; a shared privileged account is a weakness. The service consequence explains why the department should act.

Use the actual operating context. Identify exposed interfaces, users, dependencies and existing controls. A threat list copied from another department may omit the manual approval or supplier link that matters most in your service.

chapters.title: Assess before and after controls
chapters.bodyHtml:
Inherent risk describes the assessed exposure before the controls considered in the assessment. Residual risk reflects the controls actually operating. Target residual risk describes the intended position after a planned treatment. Do not credit a proposed control as though it already works.

Use the department's approved assessment method and explain its scales. A likelihood-impact matrix is a prioritisation aid, not an exact financial prediction. Multiplying ordinal labels does not convert them into a loss probability or a rand amount.

Assess impact across relevant dimensions: affected people, service disruption, legal obligations, financial loss, safety and trust. State the time horizon and evidence supporting likelihood. If information is weak, explain the uncertainty and identify a useful observation rather than inventing precision.

chapters.title: Prioritise by consequence and decision need
chapters.bodyHtml:
Two risks with the same matrix score can need different responses. One may threaten a critical payment tomorrow with no fallback; another may affect an internal service with a tested workaround. Explain urgency, exposure, dependencies and available temporary protection alongside the score.

The SARS example shows a public institution using a risk-based selection process to focus work. The educational lesson is to examine the method and coverage, not to import a tax-risk percentage as a cyber-risk threshold.

Keep the assessment reviewable. Record its date, service owner, evidence, control assumptions and reason for priority. A later reviewer should be able to explain why the department chose an action, including what was unknown at the time.

application.title: Assess three relief-service risks
application.instructionsHtml:
Fictional case: the payment platform has a shared supplier administrator account; district connectivity is unreliable but an approved offline intake process exists; a new analytics export is planned but not yet enabled.

Use a stated four-level likelihood and impact scale. Spend about 60 minutes writing three risk statements, identifying current controls, residual-risk reasoning and the next decision.
application.deliverable: A three-row risk register with assumptions and priorities.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
For privileged access, connect the weakness to unauthorised payment change and citizen harm. For connectivity, consider the demonstrated coverage and limits of offline intake. For the planned export, distinguish current exposure from the change that would create it.

Do not count proposed named access or a future second connection as an existing control. State the evidence and review trigger.

Different rankings can be defensible if the scale, assumptions, consequences and urgency are clear. Unsupported numbers without reasons are not a sufficient assessment.

reflection.prompt: Which risk score in your register would be hardest to explain to its service owner?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Rewrite the statement and identify the evidence behind its current rating.

quiz.title: Describe and assess the service risk — knowledge check

questions.name: M07-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which is the strongest risk statement?

answers.textHtml: A shared privileged account could enable unauthorised payment changes, delaying relief
answers.feedbackHtml: Connect condition, event and service consequence.

answers.textHtml: The department has computers
answers.feedbackHtml: That is an asset fact without an uncertain event or consequence.

answers.textHtml: Cyber risk is unacceptable
answers.feedbackHtml: That is a judgement without the risk's cause and effect.

answers.textHtml: The supplier must install a new tool
answers.feedbackHtml: That is a proposed treatment, not the risk statement.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Connect condition, event and service consequence.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A named-access control is approved but not implemented. How should it affect residual risk?

answers.textHtml: It belongs in target residual risk, not as an operating current control
answers.feedbackHtml: Distinguish present controls from planned treatment.

answers.textHtml: Count it immediately because funding is approved
answers.feedbackHtml: Approval does not establish operation.

answers.textHtml: Remove the risk because a plan exists
answers.feedbackHtml: The current exposure remains.

answers.textHtml: Ignore the plan entirely
answers.feedbackHtml: It is relevant to treatment and target risk.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Distinguish present controls from planned treatment.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What does a four-by-four likelihood-impact score directly provide?

answers.textHtml: A prioritisation result within the defined assessment method
answers.feedbackHtml: Use the matrix within its defined meaning.

answers.textHtml: An exact probability of loss
answers.feedbackHtml: Ordinal scales do not establish that.

answers.textHtml: A rand loss amount
answers.feedbackHtml: No monetary model is supplied.

answers.textHtml: Proof that equal scores have equal urgency
answers.feedbackHtml: Service context and timing can differ.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use the matrix within its defined meaning.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: Two risks have the same score, but only one threatens tomorrow's essential payment. What should the decision include?

answers.textHtml: Urgency, service consequence and available fallback
answers.feedbackHtml: Scores support, rather than replace, judgement.

answers.textHtml: Treat them identically because the numbers match
answers.feedbackHtml: The score omits relevant context.

answers.textHtml: Always prioritise the larger technical system
answers.feedbackHtml: System size is not the same as consequence.

answers.textHtml: Delete the lower-urgency risk
answers.feedbackHtml: It may still need treatment.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Scores support, rather than replace, judgement.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: Which evidence most strengthens an availability-risk assessment?

answers.textHtml: Observed outages and the tested coverage of the fallback process
answers.feedbackHtml: Use actual service and control evidence.

answers.textHtml: A generic sector headline alone
answers.feedbackHtml: It may not describe the local service.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's unqualified assurance
answers.feedbackHtml: Its scope and evidence need assessment.

answers.textHtml: A planned recovery exercise next year
answers.feedbackHtml: That is not current recovery evidence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use actual service and control evidence.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: How should the SARS risk-selection case be used here?

answers.textHtml: As an example of risk-based prioritisation with a defined scope
answers.feedbackHtml: Keep the case within its actual domain.

answers.textHtml: As a mandatory departmental cyber-risk threshold
answers.feedbackHtml: Tax-selection coverage does not set that threshold.

answers.textHtml: As proof that automation removes judgement
answers.feedbackHtml: Methods and results still need oversight.

answers.textHtml: As proof that every unselected case is safe
answers.feedbackHtml: Selection is not universal assurance.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Keep the case within its actual domain.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which are consequences rather than control descriptions? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Eligible residents receive late relief
answers.feedbackHtml: This is a service effect.

answers.textHtml: An unauthorised payment causes financial loss
answers.feedbackHtml: This is an impact.

answers.textHtml: Privileged access is reviewed monthly
answers.feedbackHtml: This describes a control.

answers.textHtml: Backups run nightly
answers.feedbackHtml: This describes an operating measure.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Risk consequences explain harm or lost service value.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which assessment records support later review? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Evidence and control assumptions
answers.feedbackHtml: They explain the rating.

answers.textHtml: Date, owner and time horizon
answers.feedbackHtml: They place it in context.

answers.textHtml: A score with no scale definition
answers.feedbackHtml: Its meaning cannot be assessed.

answers.textHtml: A future control represented as already operating
answers.feedbackHtml: That overstates current protection.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Retain the basis of the assessment.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Weak evidence should be made explicit rather than converted into an invented precise probability.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Uncertainty is part of a useful decision record.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Uncertainty is part of a useful decision record.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Uncertainty is part of a useful decision record.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A threat, a vulnerability and a service consequence are interchangeable terms.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. They describe different parts of the risk.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: They describe different parts of the risk.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: They describe different parts of the risk.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the term to its meaning.

pairs.answer: Information or capability supporting the service
Risk after the controls currently considered

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Clear terms help keep the assessment coherent.

questions.name: M07-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A complete risk links a cause, an uncertain [[1]] and a service [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The statement explains what could happen and why it matters.

units.title: Treat, accept and monitor risk
objectives: Compare treatment options and residual effects.
Assign accountable acceptance and review conditions.
Monitor whether treatment changes the service exposure.

chapters.title: Choose a treatment that addresses the cause
chapters.bodyHtml:
Treatment options include reducing exposure or impact, avoiding a discretionary activity, sharing defined financial or service responsibilities, and retaining risk within authority. These options have limits. Insurance does not restore a missed public service, and outsourcing does not erase departmental accountability.

Compare the control with the actual risk statement. If unauthorised payment changes are the concern, a general awareness poster alone will not replace restricted access and independent change approval. Training may support the process, but the treatment must reach the cause and consequence.

State cost, implementation time, dependencies and new risks. A control that blocks all district access may reduce one exposure while preventing legitimate decisions. Consider a service-preserving temporary measure while the durable treatment is delivered.

chapters.title: Acceptance is a decision with conditions
chapters.bodyHtml:
Risk acceptance should identify the risk, current controls, residual exposure, reason, authorised decision maker, scope, expiry or review trigger and monitoring. It is not a synonym for ignoring the risk or declaring it eliminated.

Use the department's appetite and tolerance arrangements to decide where acceptance is permitted and when escalation is required. A local manager cannot use an acceptance form to create authority beyond their delegation or waive a mandatory legal duty.

Review when assumptions change. A service that adds sensitive information, a control that fails or a supplier that changes its support model can invalidate the basis of an earlier decision. Preserve the original acceptance and record the subsequent decision rather than overwriting history.

chapters.title: Close treatment through an observed outcome
chapters.bodyHtml:
A treatment plan needs an owner, milestones, resources and an outcome measure. Track whether the control was delivered and whether it addresses the intended exposure. A purchased licence is not the same as configured, adopted and effective access control.

Use indicators that help the owner act: unreviewed privileged accounts, overdue revocations, failed recovery steps or repeated exceptions. Define the threshold, review frequency and response. A metric without an action route becomes reporting overhead.

After implementation, reassess using the same risk definition and method. Explain what changed and what remains. If the result is weaker than expected, revise the treatment or escalate the residual decision. Retain the link from risk to decision to delivered control.

application.title: Choose a treatment for supplier payment access
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional department can buy named-access support forR120000per year, redesign approvals forR40000and two months' work, or keep shared access temporarily with daily review and independent payment approval. The critical service cannot simply stop.

Spend about 60 minutes comparing options, proposing an interim arrangement and drafting the residual-risk decision.
application.deliverable: An options table, treatment plan and acceptance record.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Assess which controls prevent or detect unauthorised change and which support attribution. Compare recurring cost, implementation time and operational burden.

A temporary arrangement can be proposed with explicit authority, scope, expiry and review, while a durable named-access/approval solution is delivered. Do not call the temporary risk eliminated.

Define closure through observed permissions and payment-change operation, then reassess residual risk. Keep legal and delegated-authority constraints explicit.

reflection.prompt: Which accepted risk has no clear review trigger?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Specify the change or threshold that should bring it back to the decision maker.

quiz.title: Treat, accept and monitor risk — knowledge check

questions.name: M07-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: What is the main limitation of insurance as a treatment for service interruption?

answers.textHtml: Financial recovery does not itself restore the public service
answers.feedbackHtml: Risk-sharing arrangements have a defined scope.

answers.textHtml: Insurance necessarily removes the department's service-delivery accountability
answers.feedbackHtml: A financial transfer does not transfer all public-service responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: An insurance policy proves that the current recovery process meets its objective
answers.feedbackHtml: Coverage is not evidence of operating recoverability.

answers.textHtml: Insurance automatically prevents the interruption from occurring
answers.feedbackHtml: Compensation arrangements do not themselves prevent the underlying event.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Risk-sharing arrangements have a defined scope.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A risk concerns unauthorised payment edits. Which treatment best addresses its cause?

answers.textHtml: Restrict editing and require independent authorised change approval
answers.feedbackHtml: The control should reach the described event and weakness.

answers.textHtml: Only distribute a general awareness poster
answers.feedbackHtml: Awareness alone does not constrain the edit.

answers.textHtml: Increase website availability only
answers.feedbackHtml: That addresses a different objective.

answers.textHtml: Rename the risk to low
answers.feedbackHtml: A label does not change exposure.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The control should reach the described event and weakness.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What does a valid risk acceptance state?

answers.textHtml: The residual exposure, authority, reason and review conditions
answers.feedbackHtml: Acceptance is an accountable decision.

answers.textHtml: That the risk no longer exists
answers.feedbackHtml: Acceptance does not eliminate it.

answers.textHtml: That no evidence need be retained
answers.feedbackHtml: The decision needs a basis.

answers.textHtml: That every related legal duty is waived
answers.feedbackHtml: The decision cannot create that authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Acceptance is an accountable decision.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A supplier changes its access model after a risk was accepted. What is needed?

answers.textHtml: Review whether the original assumptions still hold
answers.feedbackHtml: Changed conditions can require a new decision.

answers.textHtml: Keep the decision unchanged solely because it is signed
answers.feedbackHtml: Its basis may have changed.

answers.textHtml: Overwrite the old record with a new date
answers.feedbackHtml: That loses history.

answers.textHtml: Assume every change is automatically unacceptable
answers.feedbackHtml: Assess the actual consequence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Changed conditions can require a new decision.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What best supports treatment closure?

answers.textHtml: Evidence that the implemented control changes the intended exposure
answers.feedbackHtml: Close against the agreed operating outcome.

answers.textHtml: A purchase order alone
answers.feedbackHtml: Purchase is not operation.

answers.textHtml: A project meeting attendance list
answers.feedbackHtml: Attendance does not demonstrate the result.

answers.textHtml: A supplier's future roadmap
answers.feedbackHtml: That is a plan, not current delivery.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Close against the agreed operating outcome.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: A department is legally required to deliver a service. How should 'avoid risk by stopping it' be assessed?

answers.textHtml: Against the legal mandate and feasible service alternatives
answers.feedbackHtml: Treatment options must respect the service's authority.

answers.textHtml: Treat avoidance as automatically available
answers.feedbackHtml: A mandatory service cannot simply be abandoned.

answers.textHtml: Assume only one technical design is permitted
answers.feedbackHtml: Alternative lawful designs may exist.

answers.textHtml: Remove the service from reporting
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not discharge the mandate.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Treatment options must respect the service's authority.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which inputs belong in an option comparison? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Cost, delivery time and dependencies
answers.feedbackHtml: These affect feasibility.

answers.textHtml: Residual impact and new service risks
answers.feedbackHtml: Controls can create trade-offs.

answers.textHtml: Only the lowest purchase price
answers.feedbackHtml: That omits the full effect.

answers.textHtml: An assumed perfect result with no evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: That overstates value.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Compare options on a common service basis.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which features make a risk indicator actionable? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A defined threshold and response owner
answers.feedbackHtml: They connect measurement to action.

answers.textHtml: A review frequency and reliable source
answers.feedbackHtml: They support timely interpretation.

answers.textHtml: A number without a population or period
answers.feedbackHtml: Its meaning is unclear.

answers.textHtml: A rule that adverse trends must be hidden
answers.feedbackHtml: That prevents useful governance.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Indicators should trigger an appropriate decision.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Outsourcing a control removes the department's need to understand its residual service risk.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. The department still needs an accountable view of the service and supplier dependence.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: The department still needs an accountable view of the service and supplier dependence.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The department still needs an accountable view of the service and supplier dependence.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A treatment should be reassessed against the original risk definition after implementation.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This shows what actually changed and what remains.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. This shows what actually changed and what remains.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: This shows what actually changed and what remains.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the treatment concept to its example.

pairs.answer: Do not launch a discretionary unsafe feature
Contract for a specified recoverable financial responsibility
Accept documented residual risk with review

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Each option has a scope and does not erase all other obligations.

questions.name: M07-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Risk acceptance records residual [[1]] and a future [[2]] trigger.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Acceptance retains an ongoing governance responsibility.
